newsitem.title: Switzerland: Swiss shares end down, pressured by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end down, pressured by Wall Street.

text.p: 1440 GMT - A feeble early Wall Street put Swiss shares under pressure in late trade and the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell below the important level of 3,800 points.

"The correction is fine with me", one dealer said, noting that volumes were rather low. "The market just could not continue to soar as fast as it did in the past few days", he said, adding the SMI may fall as low as 3,750 before picking up again. "But the fundamentals remain excellent", he said.
* SMI fell 0.28 percent, or 10.6 points, to 3,797.3.
* All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) down 0.2 percent, or 4.85 points, to 2,430.54 points.
Investors concentrated on Friday's U.S. PPI data, which is expected to move the market again, dealers said. Today's U.S. jobless data pressured U.S. bonds and early Wall Street trade.
* Heavily-traded Roche certificates slid 50 francs to 9,530.
* UBS bearer shares bucked the trend, adding seven francs to 1,250. Speculation about imminent restructuring moves may have had a positive effect, on trader noted.

* CS Holding fell 0.6 percent to 128 francs. Friday's shareholders' meeting will probably deal only with the group's name change, dealers said. There had been speculation earlier that CS would announce the sale of its stake in Electrowatt.
* ABB up one franc at 1,557. News that Goran Lindahl is to succeed Percy Barnevik as CEO had little effect, dealers said.

* Shares of watchmaker SMH fell more than two percent after a a sell note by Standard & Poor's Market Scope following a review of the Smart Car project. One dealer said SMH's sales estimates for Smart, a micro car developed by SMH and Germany's Daimler Benz, may be too optimistic.
* Alusuisse ended unchanged at 939 after Wednesday's losses.
* Swissair added nine franc, help by a call option.
* Second-tier insurer Berner Holding jumped 3.8 percent.
